newsitem.title: USA: Leslie estimate seen supportive corn, neutral soy.
newsitem.headline: Leslie estimate seen supportive corn, neutral soy.

text.p: CBOT traders said the Conrad Leslie-ADM Elevator survey released early Monday was supportive to CBOT corn futures and neutral to slightly bearish for soybean futures.
"The corn number looks a little friendly for corn," a trader said.

Leslie pegged 1996 U.S. corn production at 8.906 billion bushels, above USDA's September forecast for 8.804 billion. But the Leslie data was below some private outlooks for a nine billion bushel crop this year.
"The corn number is a little friendly but the weather will dominate and for now the weather looks great for harvest the next couple of weeks," another trader said.
"The bean number was very much as expected," the trader said.

Leslie's forecast for 1996 U.S. soybean production was 2.302 billion bushels, above USDA's September forecast for 2.270 billion bushels. But the Leslie outlook for soybean production was about the same as several other private forecasts.
USDA's October crop production report is slated for release Friday.
